h1: Paradee Resort — a private cove at Ao Kiu, the southern tip of Koh Samet
intro: Drive to Phe Pier, board the resort's own speedboat and ride past the crowded main beaches for about 20 minutes — to the southern tip of Koh Samet, an area called Ao Kiu. There, Paradee Resort lays out 40 pool villas with steep pitched roofs on a near-empty white-sand beach. It's a corner of Koh Samet many people don't know exists, because cars can't reach it. A 5-star luxury resort with two beaches — one for sunrise, one for sunset. Villas start from approx. THB 12,000/night.

body.html: Paradee isn't on Sai Kaew Beach or the coves where most day-trippers land. The resort sits at Ao Kiu, the southern tip of Koh Samet, the island's narrowest point — so narrow it has a beach on each side, one facing the sunrise and one the sunset. Cars can't reach it, so getting here means taking the resort's speedboat from Phe Pier. That sounds like a hassle, but it's exactly what keeps the beach quiet and genuinely private.

All 40 villas are standalone buildings with steep pitched roofs and high vaulted ceilings, each over 100 sqm. The entry-level Garden Villa sits in the garden, while the one reviews talk about most is the Beach Front Pool Villa, with a private infinity pool opening straight onto the white sand. Each has an outdoor sala for dining or lying in the sea breeze. Many reviews say you open the door in the morning and the sand and sea are right there — a feeling you don't get from ordinary stays on the island.
"From the private speedboat to and from the island to the outstanding service everywhere in the resort, this was truly one of the most wonderful holidays we've had."

What guests praise over and over is the attentive, smiling service. Small touches stick in the memory — afternoon tea served on the beach, complimentary ice cream after lunch. It's a resort that looks after guests warmly rather than being merely luxurious and cold. TripAdvisor ranks it #1 of 24 hotels on Koh Samet with 4.8 out of 5 (978 reviews), and Trip.com gives it 9.4 from 84 reviews — consistency that says a lot.

On food, most reviews say the meals are good and not overpriced for a resort of this level — fair on an island where everything has to be brought across the sea. There's a spa, an outdoor pool, kayaking and snorkelling over reefs near the beach. The overall mood leans toward calm and privacy, suited to couples, honeymooners or anyone who genuinely wants to switch off.

To be honest, the one thing guests do flag is plastic rubbish and empty bottles that wash onto the beach from other parts of the island, especially when the current pushes in — not the resort's doing, but a wider problem for these waters that the staff clear daily and still can't fully prevent. The other point is access: miss a speedboat slot and you wait for the next one, so plan your timing.

In short, Paradee suits travellers after the quietest, most private version of Koh Samet, willing to pay for calm and good service. If you want nightlife, markets or to hop between beaches often, Ao Kiu's remoteness may not fit. But if you've come to settle in for long, lazy days with the beach, a private pool and a near-empty sea — this delivers that better than anywhere else on Koh Samet.

honestSummary: Paradee is at its best for travellers who want to switch off completely and have Koh Samet to themselves — a quiet beach, spacious villas and intuitive service. Just accept that the far-tip location makes getting around harder, and the price isn't for every trip.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Paradee Resort Rayong

faq.q: Where is Paradee Resort and how do you get there?
faq.a: Paradee is at Ao Kiu, the southern tip of Koh Samet, in Mueang Rayong. Cars can't reach it, so you travel by the resort's speedboat from Phe Pier, about 20 minutes. Give your arrival time in advance and reach the pier at least 30 minutes before your boat slot.

faq.q: What are the starting prices and villa types at Paradee?
faq.a: Rates start from approx. THB 12,000/night for a Garden Villa in the garden. The popular pick is the Beach Front Pool Villa with a private infinity pool onto the beach (from around THB 22,000). Every villa is over 100 sqm. Prices vary by season and holidays, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is Paradee Resort best suited for?
faq.a: It's ideal for couples, honeymooners or anyone who wants genuine, private rest. With a no-road location at the island's tip and a near-empty beach, it leans calm rather than lively. If you want to tour several beaches or go out at night often, a stay near Sai Kaew Beach may be more convenient.

faq.q: What awards or scores does Paradee have?
faq.a: Paradee scores 9.4 from 84 reviews on Trip.com and 4.8 out of 5 on TripAdvisor, ranked #1 of 24 hotels on Koh Samet. The points praised most often are the service, the privacy and the quiet, beautiful beach.

faq.q: Is Paradee's beach clean and the water clear?
faq.a: Ao Kiu's beach is fine white sand and very quiet, but when the current pushes in, plastic rubbish can wash ashore from other parts of the island, which the resort clears daily. Water clarity depends on the season — it can be murkier when the surf is up. Overall it's still one of the prettiest beaches on Koh Samet.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book, and is cancellation flexible?
faq.a: For long weekends and high season (Nov–Feb), book 1–2 months ahead, as there are only 40 villas and the beachfront ones sell out fast. Every platform offers a Free Cancellation option — choose that first if your plans aren't firm.
